answer: Umber-Keyed Operator Lockout ties every new identity to a parent operator record that co-signs its first action. If any child identity misbehaves, the lockout freezes the parent’s entire identity set for a full epoch, so a sybil ripple costs the operator all its accounts, not just the fake one. Each falcon identity also must post a refundable deposit equal to the median epoch revenue it earned, forfeited on lockout. That makes mass registration cost the attacker the full replacement value of every identity it controls.
